A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Med-CMR study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 18 models on Med-CMR, plus error analyses, human alignment experiments and supplementary leakage measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: The benchmark curation, question generation, filtering procedures and DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp scoring framework are unchanged. Removing a figure-reference sentence does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20,653 questions, seven task categories, 11 body systems and 12 imaging modalities. The supplementary coverage tables and evaluation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 evaluate the same 18 models, and the targeted comparisons and leakage experiments retain their comparator sets. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, scoring weights, model configurations and prompts remain unchanged. Both versions retain the 500 reformulated MCQs, 200 human-alignment samples, and leakage sample of 2,000 MCQs plus 500 open-ended questions.

E4.justification: The model-scaling analysis, GPT-5 error analysis, medical-versus-general model comparisons, human alignment study, supplementary case studies and leakage analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figures 3–4 retain the same correlation and significance reporting, including sign and Wilcoxon tests. There is no added or revised repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–5, plotted findings in Figures 3–4 and supplementary case outcomes are unchanged. For example, GPT-5 retains 57.81 MCQ accuracy and a 48.70 open-ended score.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 retains the same weighted scoring equation and weights of 1, 1, 4 and 4. No formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions, novelty claim and findings about model performance and medical specialization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of visual-grounding failures, knowledge gaps, scaling limitations and medical fine-tuning tradeoffs are unchanged. The supplementary error explanations and minimal-leakage interpretation are also retained.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same generation models, annotation procedures, VLLM/API usage, answer extraction, supplementary prompts and project-page address. Bibliographic updates do not introduce new implementation or access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven cited works, including LEMON, PointCoT, V-Skip and MedEyes, and removes ShenNong-TCM and the visual-document multi-agent framework citation. These are limited citation changes in the introduction and Section 6; the research-positioning narrative remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 deletes the sentence incorrectly describing Figure 1 as the curation pipeline. There are also terminology and bibliographic edits, but the prose and section organization are otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects 'Casual Reasoning' to 'Causal Reasoning'; its remaining visual content is identical. Text and bibliography reflow alter page layout, while the figure/table inventory, captions and structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity by correcting Figure 2's task label and removing Section 2.2's misleading reference to Figure 1 as a curation pipeline. These resolve small presentation defects; the empirical evidence, methodological support and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
